queries.hook: The wish to understand what these texts teach, and to find in them something steady to lean on.
queries.diagnose: When life is lived only for what passes, the heart feels empty; meaning is missing when we forget what does not pass.
queries.steady: What passes cannot fill the heart; turning toward what lasts gives each day a quiet purpose.
queries.act: Turn toward what lasts: serve, study, reflect daily, and offer your work to something beyond yourself.
queries.story: A story of a student who came to a teacher with questions and was led, step by step, toward the truth.

hook.speaker: Krishna
hook.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on simple, wholehearted devotion.
hook.sanskrit: पत्रं पुष्पं फलं तोयं यो मे भक्त्या प्रयच्छति । तदहं भक्त्युपहृतमश्नामि प्रयतात्मनः ॥
hook.line: A leaf, a flower, a fruit, a little water: whatever is offered with love, I accept.
hook.translation: Whoever offers me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water, that offering of love from the pure-hearted I accept.
hook.why: Small offerings given with love matter; no one is beyond turning around.

alternates.speaker: Krishna
alternates.setting: Krishna on devotees who find joy together and the light he gives them.
alternates.sanskrit: मच्चित्ता मद्गतप्राणा बोधयन्तः परस्परम् । कथयन्तश्च मां नित्यं तुष्यन्ति च रमन्ति च ॥
alternates.line: Their minds on me, they talk of me with each other, and find joy and contentment in it.
alternates.translation: With minds fixed on me and lives given to me, enlightening one another and always speaking of me, they are content and delighted.
alternates.why: Good company and an inner lamp clear the dark.

alternates.speaker: Krishna
alternates.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the power of understanding to end confusion and guilt.
alternates.sanskrit: तद्विद्धि प्रणिपातेन परिप्रश्नेन सेवया । उपदेक्ष्यन्ति ते ज्ञानं ज्ञानिनस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः ॥
alternates.line: Learn from those who have seen the truth: approach with humility, ask real questions, and serve.

alternates.why: Learn humbly, trust the process, and cut through doubt to act.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on simple, wholehearted devotion.
verse.sanskrit: पत्रं पुष्पं फलं तोयं यो मे भक्त्या प्रयच्छति । तदहं भक्त्युपहृतमश्नामि प्रयतात्मनः ॥

verse.translation: Whoever offers me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water, that offering of love from the pure-hearted I accept.
verse.why: Small offerings given with love matter; no one is beyond turning around.

prasang.title: The glory of selfless devotion
prasang.summary: A leaf, flower, fruit or water offered with love is accepted. Offer everything you do; the divine hates no one, and even a wrongdoer who turns wholeheartedly is counted good.
prasang.lesson: Small offerings given with love matter; no one is beyond turning around.

verse.meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna on the battlefield, where Arjuna is frozen by grief and moral confusion. Krishna tells him that the divine does not demand grand rituals or wealth. A simple leaf, a flower, a fruit, or a little water, given with a pure heart and love, is fully accepted. The point is that no one is beyond turning around. Even a wrongdoer who turns wholeheartedly is counted good, because the offering is not in the size of the thing but in the love behind it.
verse.for_you: You have spent decades building a life that ran on its own momentum. Now that the engine is quiet, you do not know what to put on the altar. The texts say the divine does not ask for your whole career, your reputation, or your old plans.
verse.try_today: Offer one small thing with full attention and no expectation of return.
verse.scene_line: You stand at the edge of a quiet field, holding a single leaf.
asks: What can I offer that is truly mine?
How do I know if my heart is pure enough?

verse.speaker: Rama
verse.sanskrit: दिवसास्ते महान्तस्ते संपदस्ताः क्रियाश्च ताः । सर्वं स्मृतिपथं यातं यामो वयमपि क्षणात् ॥
verse.line: Those days, those people, that wealth, those deeds are memories now. We too will pass soon.
verse.translation: Those days, those great people, that wealth, those deeds: all have passed into memory. We too will go in a moment.
verse.why: Naming honestly what feels empty is the first step; Rama's lament is a question, not the answer.
verse.misuse: Not a call to despair; it wakes Rama up to what matters now.

prasang.title: Rama's lament: what is the point of all this?
prasang.summary: Asked to speak, Rama pours out what he has seen: wealth hardens people, life drips away like water off a leaf, ego and craving run us, the mind never fills, childhood, youth and old age each bring their own suffering, and time eats everything. He ends by saying only the company of good people gives him hope.
prasang.story_hook: In front of the whole court, the young prince stood up and said what everyone feels and nobody says.
prasang.lesson: Naming honestly what feels empty is the first step; Rama's lament is a question, not the answer.

verse.meaning: After hearing the world is a dream, Rama sits with the men who raised him. He tells them that the days he lived, the friends he knew, the gold he touched, and the deeds he did are all memories now. He says they too will pass in a moment. This is his honest naming of what feels empty, not the answer, but the question that wakes him up.
verse.for_you: You are letting go of the reasons that once carried you. The quiet of retirement is not a lack, but the space where you can name what is done and what remains. See the pattern underneath the silence. The search itself is the next step.
verse.try_today: Notice one memory of your life's work and let it rest.
verse.scene_line: You stand in your quiet room, naming the days that are now memory.
asks: How do I know what is done and what remains?
How do I name what feels empty without despair?

verse.speaker: Sage Nishakara
verse.setting: The old vulture Sampati, wings burnt and grounded for ages, is told why he should live on.
verse.sanskrit: उत्सहेयमहं कर्तुमद्यैव त्वां सपक्षकम्। इहस्थस्त्वं हि लोकानां हितं कार्यं करिष्यसि॥
verse.line: You are needed exactly where you are, as you are. Your use isn't over.
verse.translation: I could give you back your wings this very day. But by staying here as you are, you will do something for the good of the world.
verse.why: Even when you feel useless, your experience may be exactly what someone needs.

prasang.title: Sampati, the bird who could not fly
prasang.summary: The despairing monkeys meet Sampati, Jatayu's old brother, whose wings burnt long ago. A sage once told him to live on, because one day his knowledge would be needed. Now he tells them Sita is in Lanka, and his wings grow back.
prasang.story_hook: For thousands of years the old bird had sat on a mountain with no wings, waiting for a reason.
prasang.lesson: Even when you feel useless, your experience may be exactly what someone needs.

verse.meaning: In the Ramayana, the old vulture Sampati sits on a mountain, his wings burnt away long ago. He has given up. A sage named Nishakara comes to him. He tells Sampati that his life is not over. He says he could restore the wings today. But he will not. He says Sampati must stay exactly as he is. His use to the world is not finished. He will do something good by remaining right where he is, without wings or flight.
verse.for_you: You have retired into a quiet that feels like the burnt wings of Sampati, no longer needed for the daily flight. The partner is there, but the old reasons that carried you have fallen away, and you are left with a sense of waiting.
verse.try_today: Notice one way your past skill helps someone today.
verse.scene_line: You are Sampati on the mountain, waiting without wings, and the world needs your view.
asks: How do I know my use is not finished?
What does it mean to be needed exactly as I am?

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on why even the fulfilled keep working for the world.
verse.sanskrit: यस्त्वात्मरतिरेव स्यादात्मतृप्तश्च मानवः । आत्मन्येव च सन्तुष्टस्तस्य कार्यं न विद्यते ॥
verse.line: One who is content and delighted in their own self has nothing left to prove.
verse.translation: But for the person who delights only in the self, is satisfied with the self, and content in the self alone, there is nothing that must be done.
verse.why: People copy what you do, not what you say; keep showing up.

prasang.title: Even the wise, even God, act for the world's sake
prasang.summary: The one content in the self has nothing left to gain, yet the wise, like Janaka and Krishna himself, keep working because others follow their example.
prasang.lesson: People copy what you do, not what you say; keep showing up.

verse.meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna that a person satisfied with their own self has nothing left to prove. The wise and the divine still act for the sake of the world. They do not work for gain. They work because others look to their example.
verse.for_you: You do not need to prove your worth to the world anymore. Your partner sees the steady life you have built. Let your presence be the example now. You are the root they still drink from.
verse.try_today: Notice one small act of showing up for your partner today.
verse.scene_line: You stand in the quiet after the work is done, and the world still looks to your example.
asks: How do I know when to act and when to rest?
What does showing up look like for me now?
Is my contentment enough, or do I still need to prove it?

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna's final counsel: act with devotion, reflect, choose, and take refuge.
verse.sanskrit: चेतसा सर्वकर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्परः । बुद्धियोगमुपाश्रित्य मच्चित्तः सततं भव ॥
verse.line: Inwardly hand all your work to the divine, hold it as your goal, and keep your mind on it.
verse.translation: Mentally resigning all actions to me, holding me as the highest, relying on the yoga of understanding, keep your mind always on me.
verse.why: Reflect fully, choose freely, and set down the fear.

prasang.title: Action with devotion: surrender
prasang.summary: Krishna urges Arjuna to offer all action, warns that ego will only trip him, tells him to reflect fully and then choose, and finally to take refuge in him alone and not grieve.
prasang.lesson: Reflect fully, choose freely, and set down the fear.

verse.meaning: Krishna is in his final counsel to Arjuna, who stands between two armies on the field. The moment is heavy, and the choice is Arjuna's alone. Krishna tells them to look at their work, their life, and hand it inward. To offer it up, to hold the highest goal, and to keep the mind steady on that single point. This is not about stopping action. It is about offering the action itself, with the ego set aside. The work remains, but the weight of proving something is gone.
verse.for_you: You have spent decades proving your worth in the world. Now that the work is done, the quiet can feel like a loss. This verse does not ask you to find a new project.
verse.try_today: Offer one small action from your morning to the quiet, without asking for a result.
verse.scene_line: You stand at the edge of the field of your own life, with the past behind you and the future open.
asks: How do I offer my days without a goal to reach?
Can I rest in the work I have already done?

verse.speaker: Seer
verse.setting: Follows the call to enjoy by letting go: how to live and work.
verse.sanskrit: कुर्वन्नेवेह कर्माणि जिजीविषेच्छतꣳ समाः । एवं त्वयि नान्यथेतोऽस्ति न कर्म लिप्यते नरे ॥
verse.line: Do your work and wish to live a full hundred years. Done in this spirit, action does not cling.
verse.translation: Doing your work here, you may wish to live a hundred years. For you there is no other way than this: done in this spirit, action does not cling to a person.
verse.why: Hold what you have lightly, keep working, and see yourself in everyone.

prasang.title: The Isha: enjoy by letting go
prasang.summary: Eighteen verses that open by saying everything belongs to the divine, so we should enjoy it without grasping. They go on to say we should work a full life without being bound, and see ourselves in all beings.
prasang.lesson: Hold what you have lightly, keep working, and see yourself in everyone.

verse.meaning: The Seer is speaking to the reader, right after the text has said that all this world belongs to the divine. The Seer is answering the question of how to live. They say you could do your work and wish to live a full hundred years. The point is that there is no other way to live than to do your work, but to do it in a spirit of letting go. When you do your work this way, your actions do not cling to you. They do not stick to your soul.
verse.for_you: The reasons that carried you through your working years are memories now, and they too will pass. You are needed exactly where you are, as you are. Your use is not over.
verse.try_today: Do one small, ordinary task for someone else without asking for thanks.
verse.scene_line: You are at the kitchen table with a cup of tea, and the morning light is waiting for you to begin.
asks: How do I let go of the past without losing my history?
What does it mean to do work when I have no job?
How do I see myself in a stranger I pass on the street?

story.title: Shabari's long wait
story.story_hook: Her teachers had all gone, and still she gathered fruit every day for a guest who had never come.
story.summary: The old ascetic woman Shabari has lived for years at Pampa after her teachers died, told that Ram would one day come. She has kept gathering forest food for him. When he arrives, she welcomes him, shows him her teachers' forest, and departs in peace.
story.lesson: Faithful waiting, unseen by the world, is not wasted.

anchor.speaker: Shabari
anchor.setting: The old ascetic woman Shabari has waited years at Pampa for Ram, as her teachers foretold.
anchor.sanskrit: एवमुक्ता महाभागैस्तदाहं पुरुषर्षभ। मया तु संचितं वन्यं विविधं पुरुषर्षभ॥ तवार्थे पुरुषव्याघ्र पम्पायास्तीरसम्भवम्।
anchor.line: I was told you would come, so I kept gathering for you. Waiting was a kind of preparing.
anchor.translation: So the great ones told me, best of men, and for you I have gathered every kind of forest food from the banks of the Pampa.
anchor.why: Faithful waiting, unseen by the world, is not wasted.

story.for_you: Shabari did not know when the guest would come, but she kept gathering. Their long wait in the forest shows you that your own years of searching are not empty. What you are gathering now is for the right moment, even if the moment is still unseen.
